messages.subject: velocity of colorbar guide
parts:
When using log transformation on certain data, the spacing of the labels on the color bar can become a little strange. E.g.

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
d <- #A data frame. Note that color has a few values one order of magnitude bigger than the others. Suppose these outliers are of interest. 
data.frame(y = rnorm(100, 1)*1:50
, x = c(1:50, 1:50)
, color = c(sample(1:10, 10, replace = TRUE), sample(1:10*100, 10)))

A <- 
qplot(data = d, x = x, y=y, color = color, geom= "point", size = 2)+
scale_colour_continuous(guide = guide_colorbar(barheight =20), trans ="log10")+
opts(title = "Log10 transform colors") 
B <- qplot(data = d, x = x, y=y, color = color, geom= "point", size = 2)+
scale_colour_continuous(guide = guide_colorbar(barheight=20))+
opts(title = "Linear colorscale")
grid.arrange(A,B,ncol = 2)

Is it possible to adjust the rate of change of the colorbar to also be a logarithmic function of it's value? 

--
Andrew Winterman

Sorry for the vague language.

I guess I'd like the labels to be equally spaced regardless of the transformation. This could be either achieved by setting different breaks or changing the rate of change of colors for the color guide. 

I like the latter option because it seems difficult to explain logarithmic increments to a non-technical audience.
